blocks.raw: #  InTouch password security and account lockout
blocks.text: InTouch password security and account lockout

blocks.raw: InTouch protects user accounts through secure password storage and automatic account lockout after repeated failed login attempts. This page describes both mechanisms for security reviews and audit purposes.
blocks.text: InTouch protects user accounts through secure password storage and automatic account lockout after repeated failed login attempts. This page describes both mechanisms for security reviews and audit purposes.

blocks.raw: ## Password storage
blocks.text: Password storage

blocks.raw: InTouch never stores passwords in plain text. All user passwords are processed through the Zion authentication service and stored as irreversible cryptographic hashes.
blocks.text: InTouch never stores passwords in plain text. All user passwords are processed through the Zion authentication service and stored as irreversible cryptographic hashes.

blocks.raw: ### Hashing algorithm
blocks.text: Hashing algorithm

blocks.raw: Passwords are hashed using the following algorithm before storage:
blocks.text: Passwords are hashed using the following algorithm before storage:

blocks.raw:
```
hex( SHA-256 iterated 500,000 times, after an initial salted SHA-256 )
```

code.code: hex( SHA-256 iterated 500,000 times, after an initial salted SHA-256 )

blocks.raw: This approach has the following properties:
blocks.text: This approach has the following properties:

blocks.raw:
* **One-way:** The stored hash cannot be reversed to recover the original password.
* **Salted:** Each user's password is hashed with a unique salt. See [Salt storage](#salt-storage) for details.
* **Computationally expensive:** 500,000 iterations make brute-force attacks impractical.
blocks.text: One-way: The stored hash cannot be reversed to recover the original password.Salted: Each user's password is hashed with a unique salt. See Salt storage for details.Computationally expensive: 500,000 iterations make brute-force attacks impractical.

blocks.raw: ### Salt storage
blocks.text: Salt storage

blocks.raw: A **salt** is a random value added to a password before hashing. It ensures that two users with the same password produce completely different stored hashes, making large-scale attacks such as rainbow table lookups ineffective.
blocks.text: A salt is a random value added to a password before hashing. It ensures that two users with the same password produce completely different stored hashes, making large-scale attacks such as rainbow table lookups ineffective.

blocks.raw: A unique `password_salt` value is generated and stored for each user. At login, InTouch applies the same salt to the entered password and compares the resulting hash against the stored value. The salt is not an encryption key and cannot be used to recover the original password.
blocks.text: A unique password_salt value is generated and stored for each user. At login, InTouch applies the same salt to the entered password and compares the resulting hash against the stored value. The salt is not an encryption key and cannot be used to recover the original password.

blocks.raw: ### Storage location
blocks.text: Storage location

blocks.raw: Hashed passwords and salts are stored in the `loggable_users` table in Capillary's Zion-managed authentication database. Passwords are never written to:
blocks.text: Hashed passwords and salts are stored in the loggable_users table in Capillary's Zion-managed authentication database. Passwords are never written to:

blocks.raw:
* Browser `localStorage` or session storage
* Application logs
* API responses
blocks.text: Browser localStorage or session storageApplication logsAPI responses

blocks.raw: ## Account lockout
blocks.text: Account lockout

blocks.raw: InTouch automatically locks an account after a defined number of failed login or OTP attempts. This protects against brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks.
blocks.text: InTouch automatically locks an account after a defined number of failed login or OTP attempts. This protects against brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks.

blocks.raw: ### Login lockout
blocks.text: Login lockout

blocks.raw:
| Parameter                      | Value               |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------- |
| Failed attempts before lockout | 5                   |
| Lockout duration               | 30 minutes          |
| Counter reset                  | On successful login |

target.note: GFM table; watch for an empty `| |` header row

blocks.raw: If a user enters an incorrect password 5 times, their account is locked for 30 minutes. After the lockout period expires, login attempts are automatically re-enabled. The failed attempt counter resets when the user logs in successfully.
blocks.text: If a user enters an incorrect password 5 times, their account is locked for 30 minutes. After the lockout period expires, login attempts are automatically re-enabled. The failed attempt counter resets when the user logs in successfully.

blocks.raw: ### OTP lockout
blocks.text: OTP lockout

blocks.raw: OTP verification has a separate lockout counter, independent of the login lockout.
blocks.text: OTP verification has a separate lockout counter, independent of the login lockout.

blocks.raw:
| Parameter                          | Value                          |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Failed OTP attempts before lockout | 5                              |
| Lockout duration                   | 30 minutes                     |
| Counter reset                      | On successful OTP verification |

target.note: GFM table; watch for an empty `| |` header row

blocks.raw: A user can be subject to login lockout, OTP lockout, or both simultaneously if both counters have been exceeded.
blocks.text: A user can be subject to login lockout, OTP lockout, or both simultaneously if both counters have been exceeded.

blocks.raw: ### Locked account behavior
blocks.text: Locked account behavior

blocks.raw: When an account is locked, any login attempt returns an error. The user must wait for the lockout period to expire before trying again.
blocks.text: When an account is locked, any login attempt returns an error. The user must wait for the lockout period to expire before trying again.

blocks.raw: ### Lockout configuration
blocks.text: Lockout configuration

blocks.raw: Lockout thresholds (number of attempts and lockout duration) are not configurable per org at this time. The values are fixed platform-wide.
blocks.text: Lockout thresholds (number of attempts and lockout duration) are not configurable per org at this time. The values are fixed platform-wide.

blocks.raw: ### Unlocking an account
blocks.text: Unlocking an account

blocks.raw: There is no self-serve unlock flow. If a user needs their account unlocked before the lockout period expires, raise a ticket with the Capillary Product Support team.
blocks.text: There is no self-serve unlock flow. If a user needs their account unlocked before the lockout period expires, raise a ticket with the Capillary Product Support team.
